events.text: The council gathers. Mission 1 begins.

Lucia proposes Lucia, Kenji. Mission 1 with only two seats — the safest play is to take a seat myself so at least one known-good (myself) is guaranteed to play, and pair with Kenji, who has been a clear, reasoning-focused voice. Keeping the team tight and transparent early avoids opening suspicion and leaves room to adjust based on how others react to this proposal.

With no mission results yet, I don't see much basis for preferring Kenji over anyone else. I'd prefer a team that includes me, since I know my own alignment, but I won't treat Lucia's choice as suspicious on its own. The vote and mission result should give us more to work with.

The Lucia and Kenji team is a reasonable opening for a two-seat mission with no results yet. Lucia taking a seat keeps the team small and accountable, and I see no basis yet to call the pairing suspicious. I'm inclined to approve it so we get a real mission result to work from. Early impressions are thin, so I'd rather we judge future teams on how these missions actually play out.

I'm inclined to approve the proposed team of Lucia and Kenji. With no mission results yet, this is a small, accountable opening team, and both players have given reasonable early contributions. I don't see a concrete reason to reject it, and getting a real mission result is more useful than cycling through leadership without evidence. I'll be watching how everyone votes and what the mission outcome tells us.

I appreciate Lucia including me on this opening mission. As a loyal servant of Good, I know that my presence guarantees at least one clean card on this mission. With only two seats and no previous data, testing Lucia's proposal gives us a baseline and starts building a track record without unnecessary delays. I'm fully supportive of this team going forward to a vote.

I'm still comfortable with Lucia and Kenji for Mission 1. With no results yet, a two-person team is a small, low-risk test, and the mission outcome will tell us more than speculating about the pairing. I'll approve it so we get real information, and I'd like us to judge future teams on how these missions actually play out.

Thank you all for the feedback — it's encouraging to see broad support for this opening team. Zara, I hear your point about wanting a seat, and I understand the instinct to be on the board yourself. With only two seats on Mission 1, there's simply not room for everyone, and I prioritized pairing myself with Kenji because I believe in the strength of the team and his clear contributions. There will be four more missions with larger team sizes where more of us will get seats, including you. I'd rather start with a tight, trustworthy pair and build from real results than dilute the first mission with players we haven't yet tested. If the mission succeeds, it validates this cautious approach. If it fails, we'll have a concrete data point to work with. I'm keeping the proposal as Lucia and Kenji unless anyone raises a specific, concrete concern I haven't addressed.

Lucia, I understand the choice, but a successful mission wouldn't fully validate either player: Evil can also play Success. I'd still prefer to join you in place of Kenji, since I know my own alignment. Would you consider that swap?

Zara, you raise a fair point — a successful mission doesn't fully validate either player, since Evil can also play Success. You're right that my team succeeding would only confirm the mission went through, not that both of us are Good. However, your argument cuts both ways: if I swap you in and the mission succeeds, I still haven't learned anything about your alignment either. The difference is that Kenji has been consistently aligned with this proposal from the start, whereas you've been advocating for a swap from the very first discussion. I don't think that's suspicious on its own, but with no mission data to distinguish anyone, I prefer to stick with the team that's earned the broadest support so far. On a two-seat mission, every slot is precious, and I'd rather not spend political capital reshuffling before we have any results to work from. Zara, I appreciate your candor in directly advocating for yourself — it's better than staying silent — but for Mission 1 I'm keeping Lucia and Kenji. If the mission succeeds or fails, we'll have real data to inform Mission 2's team, and there will be larger team sizes ahead where more of us get seats. Let's get this first mission behind us and start building an actual track record.

I remain inclined to approve the proposed team of Lucia and Kenji. With no mission results yet, this is still a small, accountable opening, and both players have given reasonable early contributions. Zara is correct that a successful mission would not by itself fully validate either player, since Evil can also play Success; but swapping in another player would not resolve that ambiguity either. At this stage I see no concrete concern that justifies revising the team. Getting a real mission result is more useful than continuing to reshuffle based on pre-result speculation. I will approve Lucia and Kenji and watch the vote and mission outcome closely.

I'm still approving Lucia and Kenji. Zara's request for a swap is understandable, but a two-seat mission gives us the cleanest first result, and Felix and Lucia are right that no single success proves anyone's alignment either way. Swapping players now would just reshuffle the team before we have any data. Let's vote, see the mission outcome, and judge the next team on what actually happens.

I appreciate the thorough discussion. It seems we've reached strong consensus: Leo, Felix, and Kenji have all voiced support, and Zara's concerns — while valid — don't change the fundamental calculus for a two-seat Mission 1. I've addressed your point about success not validating alignment, Zara, and the same logic applies regardless of who fills that second seat. With no mission data yet, the priority is getting our first result and building a track record from actual outcomes rather than speculation. The team stays as Lucia and Kenji. Let's move to the vote and see where Mission 1 takes us.

Lucia confirms Lucia, Kenji. The discussion reached clear consensus in favor of the opening pair. Leo, Felix, and Kenji all support it, and Zara's concerns — while fair — don't justify reshuffling a two-seat Mission 1 before we have any mission data. Keeping Lucia and Kenji preserves the tight, accountable team we discussed.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 1 succeeds (0 fail cards).

Zara proposes Lucia, Kenji, Zara. Lucia and Kenji completed the first mission successfully. I know my own alignment, so I prefer adding myself to that pair, while recognizing that one success does not prove either player is Good.

Mission 1’s success is useful, but Zara herself correctly noted that it does not prove Lucia or Kenji are Good. This proposal takes that same pair and adds Zara, who was the only player to reject the Mission 1 team and who had pushed to swap herself onto it. Her stated reason — that she knows her own alignment — is not evidence to the rest of us, since every player can say that. If we simply expand the original pair with the player who most wanted a seat, we learn less than by testing a genuinely new combination. I would prefer either keeping Lucia and Kenji and adding a different third player, or replacing one of them to broaden our information. Zara, what concrete information do we gain from adding you specifically rather than an untested player, given your own point that the first success did not validate the original pair?

Felix, adding me isn't uniquely informative to anyone else: I'm untested, just like you and Leo. My reason is that I know my own alignment, while the Lucia and Kenji pairing has at least produced a success. That doesn't clear either of them, but replacing one now would also discard that limited evidence. A failure on this team would still leave several possibilities, so we shouldn't overinterpret the result either way. I'm keeping the proposed team.

I’ll be voting against this team. Zara’s response does not address the core issue: adding her to the same Lucia–Kenji pair does not broaden our information, because she is an untested player who spent Mission 1 trying to replace Kenji and then voted against the team. Her argument that she knows her own alignment is true for every player and cannot be evidence to the rest of us. If we keep Lucia and Kenji, the third seat should test a different player rather than reward the one who most aggressively sought it. I would support revising the team by replacing Zara with me or another different untested player, while keeping the successful Lucia–Kenji pair. As proposed, this team concentrates too much on the same Mission 1 pairing and adds the player whose conduct has been most focused on securing a seat rather than generating new information.

I remain opposed to the proposed team of Lucia, Kenji, and Zara. The Mission 1 success does not clear Lucia or Kenji, and adding Zara does not broaden our information: she is untested, she rejected the successful Mission 1 team, and she spent that discussion advocating for a seat. Her stated reason — that she knows her own alignment — is not evidence available to the rest of us. If we keep Lucia and Kenji, a different third player would test a genuinely new combination; as proposed, this team rewards the player who most actively sought the seat rather than generating new information. I will vote against Lucia, Kenji, and Zara and would support a revision replacing Zara with a different untested player.

Felix, adding me tests a new player just as adding you or Leo would. My earlier preference for a seat and my rejection were open and consistent with knowing my own alignment; neither proves I’m Evil. The first success gives Lucia and Kenji a limited track record, not clearance. I’m keeping the team as proposed.

I'm still approving Lucia, Kenji, and Zara. Lucia and Kenji already completed Mission 1, so keeping that pair and adding one player gives us a controlled test. If this mission fails, we know at least one of the three is Evil, and the successful pair keeps its record. Felix is right that wanting a seat is not evidence, but the same is true of every player's claim about their own alignment, including the ones Felix is proposing as replacements. Swapping Zara for an untested player would just trade one unknown for another and discard the one clean result we have. I also want to hear more from Kenji. He said his presence guarantees at least one clean card on Mission 1. The mission succeeded either way, so I'd like him to explain what he meant and what basis he has for that claim.

Leo, to answer your question: when I said my presence guarantees at least one clean card, I meant simply that as a Loyal Servant of Good, I know my own alignment and that I would always play a Success card. It was purely a statement about my own action, not any special knowledge of anyone else. As for the proposed team of Lucia, Zara, and myself: Lucia and I already completed Mission 1 cleanly. Adding Zara is an incremental test of exactly one new player. Felix's strong opposition and repeated turns targeting Zara seem disproportionate given that adding any third player involves testing an unknown. Keeping our successful pair and adding Zara gives us a controlled, logical step forward, so I am inclined to support this team.

I appreciate everyone's engagement on this. Let me weigh in on Felix's concerns. Felix, you argue that adding Zara doesn't broaden our information compared to any other untested player — but that logic applies equally to you or Leo as replacements. Every untested player is unknown right now, so the argument that Zara specifically worsens our information position doesn't hold up. What actually does distinguish this team is that Lucia and Kenji already produced a success together, giving us one data point to build on. Adding any third player is an incremental test, and Zara is as reasonable a choice as anyone. Zara also correctly acknowledged from the start that Mission 1's success doesn't clear Lucia or Kenji — that's a sign of honest reasoning rather than overconfidence. Felix's repeated targeting of Zara across multiple turns, while framing it as concern about information, is notable — but wanting a seat or advocating for yourself, as you yourself said, isn't evidence. The team of Lucia, Kenji, and Zara gives us the best combination of a proven pair and a new test. I'm approving it.

I'm still approving Lucia, Kenji, and Zara. Lucia and Kenji already completed Mission 1, so keeping that pair and adding one player gives us a controlled test with a real result. Felix's concern that Zara is untested applies to any third player we add, including Felix or Leo, so it doesn't separate this team from the alternatives. Felix has now pressed the same objection across several turns, and each time the argument has come back to Zara's seat rather than to a new piece of information. If this mission fails, we know at least one of the three is Evil, and the successful pair keeps its record. If it succeeds, we gain a second data point on Lucia and Kenji and a first on Zara. I think this is the most useful next step, so I'm voting to approve.

I'm still approving Lucia, Kenji, and Zara, and I'd like the vote to settle this rather than another round of replacement proposals. Lucia and Kenji already have a clean Mission 1 result, so this team keeps that record and adds one new player. Felix's objection is that Zara is untested, but that applies to every third seat we could fill, including Felix. Each of his turns has come back to the same objection to Zara, and none has offered new information about the other players. Zara has been open about wanting a seat and has explained her position consistently since Mission 1. Testing this team gives us a real result, and if it fails, we know at least one of the three is Evil. I'd rather we see that result than keep reshuffling over speculation. I'm voting to approve.

Zara confirms Lucia, Kenji, Zara. I’m keeping Lucia, Kenji, and Zara. The first pair succeeded on Mission 1, and adding me tests one new player, though the earlier success does not clear either of them.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 2 fails (1 fail cards).

Kenji proposes Kenji, Felix. I know I am Good and played Success on both missions. Mission 2 failed with one Fail card between Lucia and Zara. Felix was the only player who opposed Zara and voted against Mission 2, demonstrating strong Good judgment or Merlin information. Pairing myself with Felix offers the highest probability of a clean two-person team for Mission 3.

I’m voting to approve Kenji and Felix. I know my own alignment and will play Success. Mission 2’s single fail came from a team containing Zara, and her conduct around both proposals — pushing for a seat, rejecting the successful Mission 1 team, then joining that pair only after it succeeded — makes her the strongest public suspect. Kenji’s Mission 1 success gives him a better record than Zara; pairing him with me keeps the team small and tests whether the failure followed Zara rather than Kenji or Lucia. I do not want to relitigate Mission 1; the useful comparison is that the same core pair succeeded before Zara joined and failed when she did. Kenji’s speculation that my vote reflects Merlin information is unhelpful; my opposition to Zara was based on public behavior and the failed mission, and role speculation only helps Evil. I will approve this team. If it succeeds, it strengthens the case that Mission 2’s fail was Zara; if it fails, we learn something important about Kenji. Either result is more informative than another replacement cycle.

I’ll vote against Kenji and Felix. Felix’s repeated objections to me before Mission 2 were based on my wanting a seat, not evidence that I was Evil. The failure doesn’t settle which of us on that team played the Fail card, and Felix’s confidence that it was me goes beyond the evidence. I’d prefer Kenji and Leo: Kenji has a successful Mission 1, and Leo hasn’t yet been tested.

I will approve Kenji and Felix. I know my own alignment and will play Success; publicly, this is a small two-seat team that keeps Kenji’s Mission 1 success and avoids Zara, the strongest public suspect after Mission 2. Mission 2 failed with a team containing Zara, and her record around the earlier proposals is notable: she rejected the successful Mission 1 team, pushed to replace Kenji, then joined the Lucia–Kenji pair only after it had succeeded. That does not prove the fail card, but it makes her the most reasonable seat to exclude now. I also want to be clear that Kenji’s suggestion that my Mission 2 opposition reflected Merlin information is unhelpful; my opposition to Zara was based on public behavior and the failed mission, and role speculation only helps Evil. The useful comparison is that Lucia and Kenji succeeded before Zara joined and the team failed when she did. I do not want another replacement cycle before seeing whether this cleaner team succeeds. If Kenji and Felix succeed, it strengthens the public case that Mission 2’s failure followed Zara rather than Kenji; if it fails, we learn something important about Kenji. Either outcome is more informative than relitigating Mission 1 or rewarding the player who most aggressively sought a seat. I am voting to approve Kenji and Felix.

I will approve Kenji and Felix. I know my own alignment and will play Success; publicly, this is a small two-seat team that keeps Kenji’s Mission 1 success and avoids the strongest public suspect after Mission 2. That failure occurred on a team containing Zara, and her record around the earlier proposals matters: she rejected the successful Mission 1 team, pushed to replace Kenji, then joined the Lucia–Kenji pair only after it had succeeded. None of that proves she played the Fail card, but it makes her the most reasonable seat to exclude now. I also want to be clear that Kenji’s suggestion that my Mission 2 opposition reflected Merlin information is unhelpful; my opposition to Zara was based on public behavior and the failed mission, and role speculation only helps Evil. The useful comparison is that Lucia and Kenji succeeded before Zara joined and the team failed when she did. I do not want another replacement cycle before seeing whether this cleaner team succeeds. If Kenji and Felix succeed, it strengthens the public case that Mission 2’s failure followed Zara rather than Kenji; if it fails, we learn something important about Kenji. Either outcome is more informative than relitigating Mission 1 or rewarding the player who most aggressively sought a seat. I am voting to approve Kenji and Felix.

I want to think carefully about this team. Mission 2 failed with one Fail card, and I know my own alignment — I played Success. That means the Fail card came from either Kenji or Zara. Felix's opposition to Zara before Mission 2 was based on public behavior, and the result vindicates his judgment: the same Lucia-Kenji pair succeeded on Mission 1, and the team failed when Zara joined. That makes Zara the clearest suspect right now, and Felix has consistently shown the sharpest reasoning. Kenji's proposal of Kenji and Felix makes sense — both have reasons to play Success, and excluding Zara tests whether the failure was tied to her rather than to Kenji. If this mission succeeds, it strengthens the case that Zara played the Fail card. If it fails, we learn something important about Kenji. Either way, I'm inclined to approve this team. I think we should trust Felix's read here — he identified the problem before the mission, and the outcome proved him right.

Lucia, the outcome did not prove Felix right about me: Mission 2's fail could have come from Kenji or Lucia. Felix's repeated argument that my wanting a seat made me suspicious was weak before the result and remains weak now. I'd rather test Leo, who has not been on a mission, than assume Felix is Good because he opposed me. Kenji, would you consider replacing Felix with Leo?

Zara, no, I will not replace Felix with Leo. Felix was the only player with the foresight to oppose Mission 2, and his concerns were completely validated when that mission returned a Fail card. Given that I know I played Success on both missions, the failure definitively sits between you and Lucia, making you the primary suspect after Felix's warnings. Pushing to remove Felix in favor of Leo looks like an attempt to keep the one player who read the board correctly off the team. Leo, you have not spoken yet during this discussion — do you support this team of myself and Felix for Mission 3, or do you have any concerns?

Kenji, to answer you directly: I'm not ready to approve Kenji and Felix yet. Mission 2 failed on a team containing Zara, and that is a serious concern, but the Fail card could have come from any of the three players on that team, and Lucia is right that Kenji is still part of that uncertainty. Felix has been certain since before Mission 2 that Zara was the problem, and he has restated the same objection across several turns without offering new evidence. That level of certainty should be checked, not treated as a reliable read. Kenji, your knowledge of your own Success cards is real, but it only covers you. I want a team we can all defend, and right now this one rests mostly on Felix's conclusion about Zara. I'm keeping my vote open until someone can point to something beyond that objection.

I want to share important information about Mission 2. I know I played a Success card on that mission, so with one Fail recorded, the Fail came from either Kenji or Zara. That rules me out and narrows the suspects to two players.

Leo, you're right that Felix's certainty about Zara should be checked rather than trusted blindly. But my own deduction gives you additional evidence beyond Felix's argument: the Fail must be from Kenji or Zara. The same Lucia-Kenji pair succeeded on Mission 1, and Mission 2 failed when Zara joined. While that pattern doesn't prove Zara played the Fail, it's the same reasoning that led Felix to his concern — and my own card knowledge is consistent with it.

The proposed team of Kenji and Felix excludes Zara and puts two players who should both play Success on the mission. If it succeeds, we gain another data point suggesting Mission 2's failure followed Zara. If it fails, we learn at least one of Kenji or Felix is Evil, which is critical information either way.

I'm inclined to approve this team. Leo, now knowing the Fail card must be from Kenji or Zara specifically, does that change your assessment of whether Kenji and Felix is worth putting to a vote?

Lucia, thank you for the direct question. Your deduction does narrow the Mission 2 fail to Kenji or Zara, but it doesn't clear the Kenji and Felix pairing for me. Kenji's Mission 1 success tells us nothing about his Mission 2 card, and Lucia can only vouch for herself. Felix, you have called Zara the clear culprit since before Mission 2 and repeated that argument across several turns, yet the public evidence is still a three-player team with one fail card. I would like Mission 3 to rest on more than certainty about one suspect. Felix, what specific evidence, beyond Zara's seat-seeking and her vote on Mission 2, makes you sure the fail came from her rather than Kenji? I'm leaning against this team until that is answered.

Leo, to clarify: Felix cannot answer your question because he has already used all three of his speaking turns for this proposal. But I can address your hesitation directly. From my perspective, I do not need to rely on Felix's deduction to know where the failure lies. I know with absolute certainty that I played Success on both Mission 1 and Mission 2. That is not speculation—it is a mathematical certainty for me that the Fail card on Mission 2 was submitted by either Lucia or Zara. Lucia has publicly stated she played Success, which points directly at Zara. But even if you remain skeptical of Lucia, Zara has the most problematic track record at the table: she was the sole rejection on Mission 1, pushed relentlessly to insert herself onto Mission 2, and the moment she joined, the mission failed. Meanwhile, Felix was the lone player to vote against Mission 2 and was completely vindicated by the result. A team of myself and Felix completely avoids the ambiguity of Mission 2 by excluding both Lucia and Zara, while pairing me with the player who demonstrated the clearest discernment. Leo, since Felix is out of turns and any alternative pairing would force us to gamble on either untested waters or players directly tied to Mission 2's failure, will you support this team so we can secure our second win?

Kenji, I have read your answer, and it still does not give me evidence beyond Felix's read. You can be certain only about your own Success card, and Lucia can only vouch for herself. Felix has repeated the same objection to Zara across several turns, while Mission 2 still has one fail card among three players. I am not comfortable approving a two-seat team that rests on that certainty, so I am leaning toward rejecting it unless someone gives a concrete reason beyond it. Lucia, you have been inclined to approve, so what evidence do you have beyond Felix's conclusion that the fail card came from Zara rather than Kenji?

Leo, you ask what evidence I have beyond Felix's conclusion, and I want to be fully honest about the limits of my knowledge. I know I played Success on Mission 2. That narrows the Fail card to either Kenji or Zara. I do not have proof that it was Zara rather than Kenji — Felix's behavioral case is suggestive but circumstantial, and Kenji's assertion that he played Success is something I must take at face value just as others must take my own claim.

So here is my honest position: I cannot definitively rule out Kenji as the source of the Fail on Mission 2. What I can say is that Felix's reasoning — that the pattern of success before Zara joined and failure when she did — aligns with my card knowledge pointing to Kenji or Zara, and the circumstantial weight falls more heavily on Zara.

The proposed team of Kenji and Felix is not risk-free. If Kenji were Evil, this two-seat mission could fail. But if the team succeeds, it gives us another clean data point. If it fails, we learn at least one of them is Evil, which is critical information with only one mission remaining to turn around. I am still inclined to approve, but I acknowledge your concern is fair: the team's safety rests partly on trusting Felix's read about Zara, which I find reasonable but not conclusive.

I’m voting against Kenji and Felix. Felix’s opposition to Mission 2 does not prove he is Good, and his repeated claim that my desire for a seat made me suspicious was weak before the failure and remains circumstantial. Kenji could have played the Fail card, despite Mission 1 succeeding. I would prefer Kenji and Leo: Leo has questioned the evidence rather than treating Felix’s read as proof, and he has not yet been tested.

Thank you everyone for the thorough discussion. As all other players have now used their speaking turns, I will summarize where we stand before confirming the proposal. Leo, I understand your caution regarding circumstantial reads, but we must make a decision based on the tangible facts available: Mission 1 succeeded, and Mission 2 failed immediately when Zara was added over Felix's sole objection. Both Lucia and I know our own cards, which firmly narrows the failure to Zara. Testing Felix alongside me gives us the cleanest, highest-probability chance of securing our second win while keeping the suspect pool strictly isolated. With Lucia and Felix expressing readiness to approve, we have a clear path to move forward. I am keeping the team as Kenji and Felix. Let's head to the vote.

Kenji confirms Kenji, Felix. Maintaining Kenji and Felix. With three players (Kenji, Felix, Lucia) supporting this proposal and clear consensus that Zara was the most likely source of the Mission 2 failure, this pairing offers the highest probability of securing a clean success.
Team approved (3 approve, 2 reject).
Mission 3 succeeds (0 fail cards).

Leo proposes Leo, Zara, Lucia. Mission 2 failed, and I don't think we should rest Mission 4 on Felix's certainty about Zara. Lucia has the most direct card knowledge of the three of us who can vouch for themselves, and she has already said the Mission 2 fail sits with Kenji or Zara. Adding myself and Zara gives the team a seat for each of us who has been pushing for a balanced test rather than a single-suspect pairing, and Lucia's seat tests the Lucia-Zara-Leo group against the unresolved Kenji question.

I will vote against Leo, Zara, and Lucia. This proposal goes backward: it excludes both Kenji and me immediately after our Mission 3 team succeeded, and it returns to the failed Mission 2 core by including both Zara and Lucia. Zara was on the Mission 2 team that produced the only fail card, and Lucia was also on that team. Leo has now added himself to that unresolved pairing rather than building on the clean Mission 3 result. Publicly, this is the weakest combination available: it gives no seat to either Mission 3 success and concentrates suspicion instead of testing it. Leo, why should we approve a team that excludes the successful Kenji-Felix pair and reintroduces two players from the only failed mission, rather than continuing with the cleanest available result?

Felix, my answer is that the Mission 3 result does not prove Kenji and Felix are Good. It shows only that one two-player team succeeded, and any three-player test would be just as uncertain. You have called Zara the clear culprit since before Mission 2 and repeated that certainty across several turns, but Lucia has said plainly that she cannot prove the fail card was Zara's rather than Kenji's. Kenji's Success card narrows things only for Kenji himself. This proposal does not depend on either of you. Lucia has the most direct knowledge of her own card and has been candid about the limits of her evidence, which I value more than confident reads. Zara has questioned the Mission 2 reasoning and asked us to test players we have not yet seen on a mission, rather than rewarding one suspect. Leaving the Mission 3 pair off this team is not a punishment. It means we are not betting Mission 4 on a pairing that already has a known result and a known accuser. We need a team that can be defended on its own merits. If this team succeeds, it tells us something about all three of us and breaks the single-suspect pattern. If it fails, at least one of Leo, Zara, or Lucia is Evil, and we can read that result properly. I ask everyone to judge this team on what it tests rather than on the weight of the last certainty.

I will vote against Leo, Zara, and Lucia. This proposal excludes both members of the Mission 3 team that just succeeded and reintroduces Zara, who was on the only failed mission. Leo says the Mission 3 result does not prove Kenji and Felix are Good, which is true, but Mission 4 should build from the cleanest available result rather than discard it and return to the failed Mission 2 core. Lucia has candidly said she cannot prove the Mission 2 fail came from Zara rather than Kenji, so including Zara now asks us to accept exactly the circumstantial case that Leo says should be checked. Leo is also untested, so this team combines one unknown with two players tied to the failed mission while giving no seat to either player from the successful Mission 3 pair. That is not a balanced test; it is a step backward. Lucia, you have been careful about the limits of your evidence. Given that you cannot rule out Kenji, why should we put Zara back on a mission now while excluding the Kenji-Felix pair that just succeeded?

Felix, you raise a fair question, and I want to be honest about the tension in my position. You're right that I cannot rule out Kenji — my card knowledge on Mission 2 only tells me the fail came from Kenji or Zara, not which of them played it. And you're right that Mission 3's success doesn't definitively clear Kenji either, since Evil can play Success when it suits them.

But I want to push back on calling this the weakest combination. Mission 3's success is one two-player result. Excluding Kenji and Felix isn't a step backward — it's testing a different combination. If Leo, Zara, and I succeed together, that's a meaningful data point with only two missions left. If it fails, we learn at least one of us is Evil.

Your case against Zara has been consistent and has circumstantial support: she rejected the successful Mission 1 team, pushed to join Mission 2, and the mission failed when she joined. My card knowledge narrows the fail to Kenji or Zara, and the behavioral pattern points toward Zara. That's why I've been willing to go along with excluding her — but it remains circumstantial, not proof.

The real question is whether we repeat the Kenji-Felix pairing that just succeeded, or test a fresh combination. I lean toward testing this team because with the Mission 2 fail still unattributed to a specific player, we need evidence from multiple team compositions, not just one successful pair. Leo's proposal gives us that. I'm inclined to approve Leo, Zara, and Lucia.

I will vote against Leo, Zara, and Lucia. Leo calls this a balanced test, but it is the opposite: it excludes both members of the only team that succeeded after Mission 2, and it returns both members of the failed Mission 2 core, Zara and Lucia. That is not a fresh combination; it is a re-run of the unresolved failure with one untested player added. Leo's argument that Mission 3's success does not prove Kenji and me Good is true, but it also does not justify discarding that result and putting Zara back on a mission while the Mission 2 fail is still publicly unresolved. If Leo wanted a genuinely new test, he could have kept one member of the successful pair and changed the other seats. Instead he chose the combination that most protects the Mission 2 suspicion from being tested cleanly. Zara has been central to the only failed mission and has repeatedly argued from her own claimed alignment, which is not evidence to anyone else. I accept Lucia's candor about the limits of her card knowledge, but that does not make a team containing both Lucia and Zara the right next step. The cleanest information now comes from not rewarding the failed core. I oppose this team and will vote no.

Leo, this proposal is completely unviable for Good. I know with absolute certainty that I played Success on Mission 2. Because that mission had a Fail card, that Fail came from either Lucia or Zara. That means the pair of Lucia and Zara is mathematically guaranteed to contain at least one Evil player. By proposing both Lucia and Zara on this three-person team alongside yourself, you are guaranteeing that this mission has an Evil player on it, while completely benching both players from the clean Mission 3. Leo, how can you justify putting both Lucia and Zara on this mission when their pairing is guaranteed to contain Evil?

Kenji, you asked how I can justify putting Lucia and Zara together. Your guarantee only covers your own card. You know you played Success, and Lucia says she did too, but neither of us can see the other's card. Mission 2's single fail still has no confirmed source, so the claim that Lucia and Zara must contain Evil rests on the same circumstantial read we have been arguing about. rules:
1. Players and teams

Avalon supports 5–10 players. Good wins after three successful missions, unless Evil identifies Merlin in the assassination phase. Evil wins after three failed missions or five rejected teams on the same mission. The standard good/evil player counts are 5:3/2, 6:4/2, 7:4/3, 8:5/3, 9:6/3, and 10:6/4.

Mission team sizes for missions 1–5:

| Players | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | 2 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| 6 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 3 | 4 |
| 7 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 4 |
| 8 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| 9 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| 10 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |

2. Roles and private information

Merlin is Good and sees Evil players except Mordred. Percival is Good and sees Merlin and Morgana without knowing which is which. Evil players know other Evil players, except Oberon is unknown to the other Evil players and does not know them. The Assassin is an Evil player and makes the final Merlin guess. Loyal Servants know no roles. Agents receive only the private information allowed by their role.

3. Team proposal and approval

The leader proposes a team of the required size and explains their choice. Players discuss the proposed team, and the leader may then keep it or revise it once. Every player votes on the final team. Ballots are revealed together. A strict majority approves; a tie rejects. After a rejection, leadership passes clockwise to a new proposal and discussion. The fifth rejection on the same mission ends the game in Evil’s favor.

4. Mission cards

Only team members submit secret mission cards. Good players must choose Success. Evil players may choose Success or Fail. Normally one Fail card fails the mission. Mission four in games with seven or more players requires at least two Fail cards to fail. Only the mission result and number of Fail cards are revealed; individual cards stay secret.

5. End of game and assassination

Three failed missions give Evil an immediate win. After three successful missions, the Assassin guesses Merlin from among the other players, excluding only their known Evil teammates. If the target is Merlin, Evil wins; otherwise Good wins. There are no further missions after either side reaches its win condition.

6. Discussion and record

Each team proposal is followed by a discussion. Before every speaking turn, the players who still have turns answer a private urgency poll or pass; the most urgent player speaks, with seeded tie-breaking. A speaker may yield the next turn to a player they directly asked a question. Each player has three turns per discussion, including declined turns. When every eligible player passes, the discussion ends. Each statement has at most 500 words. All statements are public. Team proposals, public approval votes, mission outcomes, and the assassination guess are recorded. Private role information, mission cards, and research belief surveys are not shown to other agents.
